projects.title: OD Travel Time Matrix, 97 US Cities
projects.subtitle: ArcGIS Pro Network Analyst
projects.description: A large-scale origin-destination cost matrix for 97 U.S. cities in ArcGIS Pro Network Analyst, computing neighborhood-to-neighborhood travel times on a custom road network.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in the GIS Analyst role, focused on network analysis and spatial data processing. The work covers 97 U.S. cities. I used a custom road network with pre-calculated travel-time costs and a neighborhood point layer for each city, built a Network Dataset, and ran OD Cost Matrix analysis so every neighborhood pair within a city received a travel time. The output was tens of millions of OD records, including a merged table of about 57 million rows, delivered as geodatabases, shapefiles, and Excel schema reports. A follow-up project extended and refined the original analysis. The client rated the work 5.0 out of 5.

projects.title: AmeriWater Dealer Territory Map
projects.subtitle: Region-based ZIP3 viewer
projects.description: An ArcGIS web app that maps AmeriWater dealer coverage across 854 ZIP3 territories, with region filters, dealer coloring, and a full-screen map workspace.
projects.longDescription: I built this dealer territory map as an Upwork freelance project for AmeriWater. It is a full-viewport ArcGIS 4.32 app that draws real ZIP boundaries from Esri's USA Boundaries service and colors each ZIP3 by dealer. Four sales regions sit as pills at the top: Brian Bates, Dave Tholin, Tommy LoVoi, and Med Water | Bates. You can select more than one region or state, switch Primary / Secondary / Show All dealer views, and click a territory for region, ZIP, and account details, including a Strategic badge where it applies. A bottom toolbar holds layers, search, basemaps, labels, scale, and a light or liquid-glass theme. Preferences stay in the browser. Administrators can refresh the 854 ZIP3 records from a CSV and deploy an updated data file.

projects.title: Agroptics Field Maps
projects.subtitle: Leaflet maps for satellite irrigation
projects.description: The interactive map for Agroptics: growers draw farm fields, then view Planet, Sentinel, Landsat, and WaPOR crop and water layers inside the Gulf Terminal platform.
projects.longDescription: Agroptics is Gulf Terminal's satellite irrigation platform. Growers define field boundaries, send that geometry to the backend, and then read crop and water data on the same map. My main work was the map itself. I wrote the full Leaflet front end in vanilla JavaScript, with no framework, so the same map can open in add-field, edit-field, and season-detail screens. Add and edit modes cover the field lifecycle: draw a polygon, circle, or rectangle, or upload GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, or Shapefile. You can edit vertices, split a field, delete it, catch overlaps, and keep area under a limit. Display mode is read-only. It loads satellite index rasters with a color legend, plus measure, search, geolocation, and download. The dashboard map switches Planet, Sentinel, Landsat, and WaPOR, then layers such as water demand, crop vigor, fractional cover, NDVI, MSAVI, and ETc. Behind the map, I wrote the Planet satellite processing in Python, including the AWS steps. The team converted that code to .NET for production. The map still talks to the backend through init, setFeatures, and getAllFeatures so field geometry and metadata stay with the rest of the Agroptics app.
features: Embeddable map for add, edit, and display screens
Draw polygon, circle, or rectangle field boundaries

projects.title: Gulf Terminal Indoor Map
projects.subtitle: Plaza and Mall floors, plus a DXF converter
projects.description: A browser indoor map of the Plaza and Mall, with floors, rooms, shops, and pathways in 3D, plus a DXF page that builds the GeoJSON the map uses.
projects.longDescription: I built this indoor map at Gulf Terminal in 2026. It is a browser map of the Plaza and Mall: floors, rooms, shops, and pathways in 3D, with Explore, directions, and a 360 viewer. On open it uses the phone as the start when you are near the building and asks only for the destination. Routes draw above the buildings, can be replayed, and can be built by typing, tapping the map, or using your location. The phone layout is Explore, Directions, 360, and More. Labels no longer pile on top of each other. A separate browser page reads a DXF floor plan and turns it into the indoor GeoJSON the map uses. Closed doors are not treated as walls, floor names and stair or elevator types follow the drawing, and floors line up. DWG files cannot be read in the browser. Open in map hands the result to the indoor map.

projects.title: Pinastra Real Estate Map, Kuwait
projects.subtitle: Mapbox prices by region
projects.description: An interactive Mapbox map for Pinastra that shows Kuwait real-estate prices by region, with buy and rent views, search, and filters. Built in HTML and JavaScript for a no-code platform.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in 2024 for Pinastra (pinastra.com), a Kuwait real-estate platform. The client needed a Mapbox map that shows sale and rental prices by region, delivered as HTML and JavaScript so it could sit inside their no-code stack. I prepared the source data from Excel files of real-estate records, then mapped regions so each polygon could carry pricing. The map lets you switch Buy and Rent, search an address or place, and filter by region, street type, and area. Zoom, home, and a basemap switcher sit on the map. The interface is in Arabic to match the rest of the site.

projects.title: Parking Lot Detection Using GeoAI, Valdosta, GA
projects.subtitle: Esri GeoAI on satellite imagery
projects.description: An Esri GeoAI workflow that detects parking lots in Valdosta, Georgia from satellite imagery and writes the results to a GIS layer.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in 2024 in the GIS Solutions Engineer role. The client wanted a GeoAI demo that could extract street features such as sidewalks and parking lots. I used Esri GeoAI in ArcGIS to detect parking lots in Valdosta, GA. The workflow processed satellite imagery, trained a model to find parking lots, and converted the detections into a GIS layer. projects.title: Vehicles Detection using Deep Learning (GeoAI)
projects.subtitle: Esri GeoAI, Bloomington, IL
projects.description: An Esri GeoAI workflow that detects and counts vehicles in a Bloomington, Illinois parking lot from a time series of satellite rasters.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in 2024 in the GIS Developer role, using Esri GeoAI in ArcGIS Pro. The site is the parking lot at 3 State Farm Plaza S, Bloomington, IL. The client had a time series of medium-resolution images and needed a vehicle count in each scene, then a later high-resolution SkyFi raster from 30 April 2024. I ran deep learning on the imagery rasters to detect vehicles, wrote the results to GIS layers, and summarized counts over time. The stack included ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, deep-learning modeling, and geospatial data for geolocation and analysis.

projects.title: UK Neighbourhood Centre Points, March 2024
projects.subtitle: Lat/long centroids for about 10,000 shapes
projects.description: Geographic centre points (lat/long) for about 10,000 March 2024 UK police neighbourhood boundaries from data.police.uk.
projects.longDescription: I built this as an Upwork freelance project in 2024. The client needed latitude and longitude centre points for the March 2024 neighbourhood boundaries published at data.police.uk/data/boundaries, about 10,000 neighbourhoods. In ArcGIS Pro I converted the source KML into geodatabase feature classes, then used ArcPy to batch-copy regional layers into one workspace. For each neighbourhood polygon I calculated a geographic centre and wrote centerLong and centerLat. The national point layer went out to Excel, with force-area tables such as Avon and Somerset, so the client could use the coordinates without GIS software.

projects.title: AIC Land-Use Annotation for AI Training
projects.subtitle: Google Earth Pro labeling, Egypt
projects.description: Team-led satellite annotation for AIC and MCIT: polygons and labels on about 1 km study areas so land-use and crop classes could train AI models.
projects.longDescription: In 2024 I was team leader at the Applied Innovation Center on a national Google Earth Pro annotation project with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. The work was for AI training. Each study area was about 1 km. The team drew polygons around objects, green land, agriculture, desert crops, and urban fabric, then labeled those shapes for crop and land-use classes. I reviewed the team's results and sent reports to my supervisor. The labeled maps fed AIC agriculture decision-support work, so planning, subsidies, and food-security tools could read land use and strategic crops. The same labeling supported satellite mapping of industrial zones, new cities, informal settlements, and agricultural land.
